sceneFacts.proactivePrompt: Is this kitchen as authentic as it looks?
sceneFacts.factHeader: The Langham kitchen was a custom-built, working set.

factBeats.text: The intense kitchen scenes were filmed on a specially constructed set at Ealing Studios, rather than in The Langham's actual kitchens.
The production designed and built the set to be a fully operational kitchen, complete with working equipment.
Chef consultant Marcus Wareing was instrumental in the set's design, drawing on his experience building real kitchens.
To make the actors appear genuinely exhausted, the stoves on set were turned on full, creating real heat and sweat.

sceneFacts.proactivePrompt: Curious about the story behind Adam's distinctive Ducati?
sceneFacts.factHeader: Adam's Ducati was a deliberate choice to define his character.

factBeats.text: Filmmakers specifically sought a 'cool high-end motorbike' for Bradley Cooper's character, Adam Jones.
The Ducati was considered essential to Adam's mode of transport and central to his rebellious style.
A brand partnership agency, Eleven.london, secured the high-end Ducati for the production.

sceneAnchor.sceneDescription: Adam is frequently seen riding his distinctive Ducati Diavel Carbon motorcycle through the streets of London, a symbol of his rebellious "rockstar chef" persona.

sceneFacts.proactivePrompt: Did you know this intense moment wasn't in the script?
sceneFacts.factHeader: Bradley Cooper Improvised This Intense Moment

factBeats.text: The dramatic moment where Adam Jones puts the sous vide bag over his head was an unscripted improvisation by actor Bradley Cooper.
Cooper revealed that the 'bag thing just sort of happened in one of the takes' during filming.
He described the experience as feeling vulnerable, but ultimately beautiful.
For Cooper, such spontaneous 'accidents' are a key reason he loves acting.

followUps: Tell me more about Bradley Cooper's acting process.
